Longevity for mice heterozygous for IGF-IR inactivation varied, with 5% to 33% increases depending on background and laboratory conditions (43‐45). This extended lifespan was only observed in the female mice. Late-life targeting of the IGF-IR with a monoclonal antibody also improved lifespan and healthspan in female mice (46). The reason for sexual dimorphism in these studies is unclear (47). Lifespan of mice lacking either the IRS-1 or IRS-2, the major intracellular effectors of IGF-IR signaling was also studied.
